title: AI-Enabled Real-Time Digital Twin System for Health Monitoring, Fault Prediction and Mission Reliability Enhancement of Aero Piston Engines used in MALE UAVs.
description:
• Background:
Medium Altitude Long Endurance (MALE) UAV are increasingly being deployed for Long-duration intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance (ISR).
Communication relay maritime surveillance and strategic defence missions Reliability and availability of propulsion systems are critical for mission success because piston-engine failures during flight may lead to mission abort, asset loss, or unsafe recovery conditions.
Conventional engine monitoring systems used in UAVs are primarily thresholdbased and reactive in nature. These systems generally indicate failures only after abnormality has already occurred. Present approaches also have limited capability to estimate remaining useful life (RUL) predict degradation trends, or simulate mission-wise engine behavior under varying environmental and operating conditions.
A Digital Twin (DT) framework for aero piston engines can significantly improve predictive maintenance, operational reliability, mission planning, and life cycle management by creating a continuously synchronized virtual representation of the physical engine using real-time sensor data physics-based models and AI/ML techniques.
The proposed problem aims to develop an indigenous Digital Twin framework suitable for deployment in MALE UAV ground control and health monitoring architecture. The solution should support real-time engine state estimation, anomaly detection degradation tracking, faultprediction, and mission replay capability.
• Description:
Develop a scalable and modular digital Twin System for an aero piston engine used in MALE UAV applications. The system shall create a real-time virtual representation of the engine by integrating.
• Engine sensor data
• Thermodynamic behavior models
• Engine performance maps
• Failure/degradation logit
• AI/ML based predictive analytics The proposed system should be capable of:
• Real-time engine parameter visualization
• Monitoring of engine health indicators
• Defection of abnormal operating conditions
• Predicting probable failures before occurrence
• Estimating degradation trends and Remaining Useful Life (RUL)
• Simulating engine behavior under different mission profiles and environmental conditions
• Supporting post-flight analysis and mission replay The system may utilize
• CAN bus/Socket CAN-based engine data acquisition
• ECU/FADEC communication interfaces Edge computing architecture Cloud or local server-based analytics
• AI/ML algorithms far anomaly detection
• Physics informed modelling approaches
• Dash board/HMI for operators and maintenance engineers
• Expected Solution:
The digital twin core framework shall act as the central intelligence layer that continuously mirrors the real aero-piston engine operating onboard the MALE UAV. The framework should establish a dynamic and continuously synchronized virtual representation of the engine using live telemetry, physicsbased models, operational history and AI-Driven analytics. The framework should be designed considering future deployment in defence grade Ground Control Station (GCS), engine test rigs, and fleet-level health monitoring infrastructures. The expected solution should include:
A. Digital Twin Core Framework
• Virtual engine model synchronized with live engine data
• Modular architecture for future scalability
• Real-time data ingestion capability B. Health Monitoring System: The health monitoring system shall continuously assess the condition of engine sub-systems and generate health indices for predictive maintenance. Monitoring of following engine parameter are required:
• RPM
• Cylinder Head Temperature (CHT)
• Exhaust Gas Temperature (EGT)
• Oil Pressure & Temperature
• Fuel flow
• Vibration signatures
• Battery Alternator health
• Injection timing parameters C. Fault Detection & Predictive Analytics: The system should transition from conventional threshold-based monitoring to intelligent predictive diagnostics. The detection/prediction of following parameters are required:
• Misfire conditions
• Injector abnormalities
• Coding degradation
• Lubrication issues
• Sensor drift/ failure
• Combustion instability
• Overheating trends
• Abnormal vibration patterns D. AE/ML Layer: The AI/ML layer shall provide adaptive learning capability for predictive diagnostic and intelligent maintenance planning. Following parameters are required to be captured:
• Anomaly detection algorithms
• Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation
• Trend analysis
• Predictive maintenance recommendations E. Simulation & Replay Capability: The system should include simulation tools to reproduce engine behavior and analyses mission scenarios. Following parameters are required to be captured:
• Replay of historical mission data
• Environmental condition simulation
• Engine behavior simulation during
• High Altitude
• Endurance mission
• Hot-weather operation
• Rapid throttle transitions F. Visualization Dashboard: The dashboard shall provide an intuitive operational interface for UAV operators, propulsion engineers and maintenance team. A user Interface displaying dashboard should support following:
• Real-time engine health status
• Fault alerts
• Engine efficiency trends
• Maintenance advisory
• Mission-wise health reports Deliverables Expected from Teams:
• Functional prototype/software demonstrator
• Digital twin architecture design
• Engine Simulation model
• AI/ML-based anomaly detection module
• Visualization dashboard
• Demonstration using simulated or real engine datasets
• Technical documentation and deployment roadmap Desired Innovation Areas: Participants are encouraged to explore:
• Physics-informed AI
• Edge AI for UAV applications
• Lightweight onboard analytics
• Hybrid thermodynamic + data-driven models
• Federated learning approaches
• Explainable AI for fault diagnosis
• Secure telemetry architecture
• Autonomous maintenance advisory systems Technical Expectations from Participants: Teams are expected to demonstrate understanding of:
• IC engine fundamentals
• UAV propulsion systems
• Sensor fusion
• Embedded systems
• CAN communication
• AI/ML analytics
• Data visualization
• Simulation modelling
• Reliability engineering
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, ml, predictive applied to a robotics and drones problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Robotics and Drones. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on sensor, model, real-time. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (4/5): built to extend across states/users with modest rework. Total 23/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: AI-Enabled Digital Twin for Aero Piston Engine Health Monitoring in MALE UAVs

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a virtual, continuously-updated replica of a UAV's engine that predicts problems before they happen, instead of the current systems that only warn you after something's already gone wrong.
overview.why_it_matters: An engine failure mid-flight on a long-endurance surveillance mission means mission abort or worse, asset loss. Predicting degradation before failure genuinely changes mission reliability.
pain_points: Conventional engine monitoring is threshold-based and reactive, indicating failure only after it occurs.
No current capability to estimate remaining useful life or predict degradation trends.
No ability to simulate mission-wise engine behavior under varying conditions.
overview.background: MALE UAVs depend on reliable piston-engine propulsion for long-duration missions, but current monitoring is reactive rather than predictive, risking mission abort or asset loss from in-flight failures.
overview.whats_being_asked: An indigenous Digital Twin framework for aero piston engines, synchronized with real-time sensor data and physics-based/AI models, enabling predictive maintenance, remaining-useful-life estimation, and mission-wise behavior simulation.
expected_solution: AI/ML-based degradation trend prediction and remaining useful life estimation.
Physics-based modeling combined with sensor data.
Mission-wise behavior simulation under varying conditions.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Breakthrough. Digital Twin frameworks for predictive maintenance are an active engineering research area; applying this specifically to aero piston engines with RUL estimation is genuine technical depth.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Combining physics-based modeling with AI/ML on real or realistic sensor data for a specific, real engine type is a substantial, specialized engineering undertaking.

competitive_landscape.note: Highly specialized aerospace predictive-maintenance PS, requires both ML and physics-based-modeling expertise, a narrow field.

innovation.note: Digital Twin plus RUL estimation for a specific engine type is genuine predictive-maintenance research territory, not a generic 'predict failure' pitch.

invention.note: Combining physics-based and AI/ML modeling together, with mission-simulation capability, is substantial technical breadth.

technical_feasibility.note: Real MALE UAV engine sensor data isn't accessible; a synthetic-but-physically-grounded dataset is the practical path.

impact_and_benefits.note: High value to a specific defense operational context (mission reliability), narrower audience than public-facing PS.

architecture.note: Physics model, AI/ML layer, and real-time data synchronization together represent genuine architectural complexity.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team with both ML and engineering/physics-modeling background. Real sensor data isn't available, but a well-grounded synthetic dataset combined with real physics-based engine modeling principles makes this genuinely demonstrable.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Very well-specified technical ask (RUL estimation, degradation trends, mission-wise simulation) gives concrete, demoable deliverables rather than vague 'digital twin' hand-waving.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building a Digital Twin that's just a data dashboard without real physics-based modeling underneath would miss the actual technical substance the PS is asking for.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Research actual piston-engine physics/failure-mode fundamentals (thermal, mechanical wear patterns) to ground your synthetic data and physics-model, rather than building a purely data-driven black-box predictor.

idea_0_4: Research basic piston engine failure modes and physics (thermal cycling, wear patterns, common failure indicators) to ground your model.
Design your synthetic sensor dataset with realistic physics-grounded degradation patterns, not random noise.
Split: one person on the physics-based model, one on the AI/ML degradation-prediction layer.
prototype_4_22: Build your physics-based engine model capturing key operational parameters (temperature, vibration, pressure trends).
Build your synthetic dataset with realistic gradual degradation leading to eventual failure.
Start the AI/ML layer for RUL estimation and degradation-trend prediction on top of the physics model.
integration_22_30: Connect the physics model, sensor data stream, and AI/ML prediction layer into one synchronized Digital Twin representation.
Test against a simulated failure-progression scenario to confirm RUL estimates behave sensibly as failure approaches.
Build the mission-wise simulation capability, testing engine behavior under varying simulated environmental/operating conditions.
polish_30_36: Build a clear dashboard showing the digital twin's real-time state, predicted RUL, and degradation trend.
Rehearse walking through a simulated degradation scenario end to end, from normal operation to an approaching failure being predicted in advance.
Prepare to discuss your synthetic data's physical grounding and what real deployment would need.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Run a simulated degradation scenario live, showing your RUL estimate decreasing appropriately as simulated wear progresses, and the system flagging a maintenance need well before actual failure, that's the concrete proof of predictive (versus reactive) capability.

strengths: Very well-specified technical deliverables give concrete, demoable targets.
Combines genuine physics-based modeling with AI/ML, real technical substance beyond a black-box predictor.
weaknesses: No real engine sensor data available, synthetic data's physical grounding is the key credibility factor.
Requires both physics/engineering and ML expertise together, a demanding combination for a hackathon team.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Balanced between physics-modeling and ML skill, this PS specifically rewards combining both, not just an ML-only approach.
team_fit.approach: Research real piston engine failure physics before generating synthetic data, this grounding is what separates a credible Digital Twin from a generic time-series predictor.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: The ML/RUL-prediction model scaffold and the dashboard visualization.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Building a physically accurate engine model and realistic degradation patterns grounded in actual piston-engine failure mechanics, that requires real mechanical engineering understanding, not assumed generic degradation curves.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI model trained on physically ungrounded synthetic degradation data would produce RUL estimates that look reasonable but don't reflect how real piston engines actually degrade, a meaningful gap for a mission-reliability tool.

data_resource_availability.status: No real MALE UAV engine sensor data is accessible to a hackathon team, this must be synthesized.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Ground your synthetic dataset in published piston engine failure-mode research and general aerospace predictive-maintenance literature, clearly labeled as synthetic but physically grounded.

judge_qna.question: How is your Digital Twin different from a standard time-series failure predictor?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Point to the physics-based model underlying your predictions, your system isn't just pattern-matching on data, it's synchronized with an actual physical representation of engine behavior, which is what makes mission-wise simulation possible.
judge_qna.follow_up: What specific physics principles does your engine model incorporate?

judge_qna.question: How confident are you in your RUL estimates given synthetic training data?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Be direct about the confidence limitation, your estimates are grounded in physically plausible degradation patterns from research literature, but real validation would need actual engine operational data and failure records.
judge_qna.follow_up: What real data would be needed to validate and calibrate this for actual deployment?
